newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-TITLE BOUT REFEREE SWITCHED AFTER TYSON PROTEST.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-TITLE BOUT REFEREE SWITCHED AFTER TYSON PROTEST.

text.p: The referee who stopped last November's heavyweight title fight to prevent Mike Tyson taking more punishment from Evander Holyfield has pulled out of the rematch following a protest by the Tyson camp, the Nevada State Athletic Commission said Friday.
Mitch Halpern's decision not to referee Saturday's World Boxing Association bout came after the NSAC had already voted at a public meeting Thursday to reject Tyson's protest.
The former champion's co-manager John Horne had argued that it was unfair to have the same man referee back-to-back title fights.
"Mike Tyson deserves fair play. This is the biggest fight of his life," said Horne, explaining that the referee issue was playing on his fighter's mental state.
A lawyer for Holyfield's camp said it had no objection to a change of referee.
However, the Commission said it was not unprecedented to have the same referee for consecutive bouts and had voted 4-1 to retain Halpern for Saturday's fight.
But there was an about-face Friday morning when NSAC Executive Director Marc Ratner told reporters Halpern would be replaced by Mills Lane for Saturday's Tyson-Holyfield WBA title fight.
"Mitch thought long and hard about the situation and felt he shouldn't be the focus of one of the greatest boxing events in the history of the sport," Ratner said.
Halpern stepped in and stopped the November 9 bout in the 11th round after Tyson was sent reeling by nine unanswered punches from the underdog Holyfield.
Despite the defeat -- only the second of his professional career -- Tyson is favoured 2-1 by Las Vegas oddsmakers to win back the heavyweight title.
